cells.detail: CAT illustrates the separate reporting layer needed to reconstruct order and trade events across participants rather than relying on public-chain visibility alone.

sources.label: SEC Rule 613 Consolidated Audit Trail overview
What information is in the CAT?

cells.text: Lifecycle event reporting to a regulatory repository
cells.note: Role in the SEC order: supporting layer

cells.text: CAT's official FAQ was updated September 23 and continues to require order, quote, routing, execution and correction events for NMS and OTC equity securities irrespective of an onchain record.
cells.detail: Where the proof stops: CAT coverage does not make blockchain events self-reporting or prove that a tokenization route has produced accepted CAT records.

items: Data + market controls · Regulatory reporting: CAT-like reporting fills the regulator-facing event ledger sublayer.
Interoperability + services · API / integration: The venue must connect its onchain and offchain event model to accepted regulatory reports.

cells.text: Regulatory reporting is not market surveillance by itself, public transaction publication, venue operation or proof of legal settlement.
cells.note: Watch: Order-specific reportable events, clocks, identifiers, linkage, correction, validation and regulator acceptance receipts.
